title: surrey-biome-pipeline: a two-extent test of scale-free climate downscaling against polygon-scale water stress

creators.name: Wang, Joshua
creators.affiliation: Independent researcher, Surrey, British Columbia, Canada

description:
Code, method and applied output for a controlled test of whether high-resolution "scale-free" downscaled climate data (ClimateBC) predicts polygon-scale vegetation water stress better than the same variables degraded to a coarse regional-model grid.

The test was run at two spatial extents. Over the City of Surrey's Green Infrastructure Network, 144 corridors digitised as 153 polygons, it was inconclusive for structural reasons: coarsening to 4 km removed only 12.3% of the predictors' spatial variance, and the climate predictors varied mostly between years while water stress varied mostly between polygons. Repeated on a 100 km Fraser Valley elevation transect spanning 4-1,920 m (300 forest stands x 4 summers), the contrast became measurable, with 48.4% of spatial variance removed at 25 km, and the direction reversed: the spatially degraded model beat the scale-free one on the point estimate in all 32 configurations tested, across cell sizes, blocking seeds and forest settings. The paired confidence interval spans zero in 31 of those 32, so the transect establishes a consistent direction rather than a resolved effect, and the difference should not be described as statistically significant. Neither model reached usable skill. Stand water stress proved near-orthogonal to the macroclimate gradient, and only local terrain and stand structure reached positive cross-validated skill.

The repository also contains the applied deliverable built after the resolution approach was shown not to work: CDEI, a Sentinel-2 and Landsat index of polygon water stress, mapped and ranked across Surrey's 144 GIN corridors and checked against Sentinel-1 radar and against ClimateBC moisture variables. The radar check does not corroborate the between-corridor ranking as water stress, so that ranking is exploratory pending ground confirmation.

Pipeline modules under src/pipeline/ each expose an importable API and a command-line entry point, and walkthrough notebooks under notebooks/ reproduce each stage end to end. All randomness is seeded (seed 26910). Source data are public and are not redistributed here, since every input is regenerable from the pipeline.

A manuscript describing this work is posted as a preprint at https://doi.org/10.32942/X2ZH5C (EcoEvoRxiv, 26 August 2026, CC BY 4.0), and it has not been peer reviewed.
notes: Generative AI tools were used in preparing this work and are disclosed in the accompanying manuscript: they were used to scaffold code and draft technical prose, which the author then revised, and as an adversarial reviewer of drafted sections. The author designed the study, ran and verified every analysis, and is responsible for all content.
